items.description: What the game must run on and how it is played (runs_on), and how it must be built (built_with). The stakeholder confirms every item.

id.description: MS-1, MS-2 and so on. Keep the id of an item you keep; a new item takes the next id above every id used before.

text.description: The requirement in plain words the stakeholder reads, on one line.

brief_quote.description: The brief's own words for this item. Empty only when proposed is true.

check.description: play when a browser can show it, command when a shell command can prove it, human when only the stakeholder can judge it.

viewport.description: For a play item: where the engine plays it.

input.description: For a play item: how it is played, or null for no input.

fits_screen.description: For a play item: whether the page must fit the viewport with nothing cut off.

how.description: For a human item: how the stakeholder checks it.

proposed.description: True when the brief does not name this item and you suggest it.

reason.description: For a proposed item: why a game like this needs it.

target_artifact.description: The document id alone, such as SPEC-M1 or TEST-PLAN-M1, with no @version or #section.

target_section.description: The slug of the heading whose text you would replace, such as risks. Name this or target_ac, not both.

target_ac.description: A criterion id, such as AC-3. On a Spec, proposed_text is that criterion's new text, which the stakeholder decides. On a Test Plan, proposed_text is that criterion's new commands, one exact shell command per line.

proposed_text.description: The whole replacement for that section, criterion text or list of commands.

proposed_verification.description: Only with target_ac on a Spec: the one shell command its Verified by line should name instead, when that command is what is wrong. proposed_text still holds the criterion's text, word for word if only the command is wrong. On a Test Plan the commands are proposed_text, so leave this out.
